name: Jacks or Better (5 Card Draw)
description: Jacks or Better: Five Card Draw. You may only open betting with at least a pair of Jacks. Prevents blind opening.

overview.description: Jacks or Better: Five Card Draw. You may only open betting with at least a pair of Jacks. Prevents blind opening.

history.origins: Five Card Draw is one of the oldest forms of poker. Jacks or Better (also called Jack Pots) emerged in the late 1800s with a minimum hand to open: a pair of jacks or better. R.F. Foster (1897) criticized the rule as injurious to poker; John Scarne (1949) argued it was essential for game stability. The variant became the most popular version of Five Card Draw.

setup.players: Two to six players; standard Five Card Draw allows this range. For Jacks or Better, at least four players are recommended so that hands are not frequently thrown in when no one can open.
setup.dealing: 5 each; open only with pair of Jacks or better.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best five-card poker hand at showdown. Betting may only be opened by a player holding a pair of jacks or better (or any hand that beats a pair of tens).
rules.gameplay: Each player receives five cards face down. Before the first bet, only a player with a pair of jacks or better (or a stronger hand) may open; others must pass. Once someone opens, remaining players may call, raise, or fold. After the first betting round, each active player may discard up to three cards and receive replacements. A second betting round follows, then showdown: the highest hand wins the pot. If the opener split openers (discarded part of the qualifying hand), those discards must be shown when the pot is awarded.
